# 2. Publish events through the message broker

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Services learn about orders by polling the order service's API every minute.
Polling adds load that grows with every new consumer, and a consumer that misses
a poll finds out late. The shipping team needs to know about an order within
seconds, and the analytics team wants every change, not only the latest state.

## Decision

We will publish an event to the message broker whenever an order is created,
changed or cancelled. Events carry the full order, and consumers subscribe to the
topics they need. The order service writes events through an outbox table, so an
event is never published for a change that was rolled back.

## Consequences

Consumers stop polling, and new consumers cost the order service nothing. We have
to version the event schema and keep old versions readable for a release. The
broker becomes something the order service cannot work without.
